section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a study examining whether self-reassurance and body-image appreciation mediate the association of social safeness and acceptance with body and eating-related psychopathology, while controlling for BMI. The study involved 309 Portuguese women who completed self-report measures. Results indicated that self-reassurance and body-image appreciation mediated the impact of social safeness on eating psychopathology dimensions, suggesting that perceiving oneself as acceptable predicts self-reassurance strategies, which in turn lead to a positive body relationship and decreased eating psychopathology symptoms.
